validated_results.title: Dairy foods, calcium intakes, and risk of incident prostate cancer in Adventist Health Study-2.
validated_results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of Adventist men reporting an adjusted hazard ratio for nondairy dietary calcium intake and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Higher (905 mg/d) vs lower (349 mg/d) nondairy calcium intake
extraction.timing: Baseline diet (FFQ) before incident cancer during average 7.8 y follow-up

sample_size.excerpt: A prospective cohort study of 28,737 Seventh-day Adventist men in the United States and Canada, of whom 6389 were of black ethnicity.

cases.excerpt: In total, 1254 (190 advanced) incident prostate cancer cases were found during an average 7.8 y of follow-up.

effect_size.excerpt: There was no evidence of an effect of higher (905 mg/d) compared with lower (349 mg/d) intakes of nondairy calcium (HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 0.94, 1.44). Men with higher intake of dairy foods, but not nondairy calcium, had a higher risk of prostate cancer compared with men having lower intakes.

confidence_interval.excerpt: There was no evidence of an effect of higher (905 mg/d) compared with lower (349 mg/d) intakes of nondairy calcium (HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 0.94, 1.44).

location.excerpt: Seventh-day Adventist men in the United States and Canada

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Diet was measured by FFQ, and 275 male participants also provided repeated 24-h dietary recalls
